recipe_version.title: Citrus Fennel Arctic Char
recipe_version.description: Roasted arctic char on sheet-pan fennel, finished with fresh dill and orange zest and juice.
recipe_version.doneness: Thickest part just opaque, flakes with a fork, 140-145 F. Not chalky. Fennel edges softened and starting to brown.

substitutions.butter: Do not swap the olive oil for butter. That would drop the dairy-free claim.
substitutions.lemon: Do not swap the orange for lemon. The citrus in this dish is orange.

ingredients.name: arctic char fillets
ingredients.note: skin-on, 5-6 oz each, about 1 inch at the thickest part

ingredients.name: fennel bulb
ingredients.note: trimmed, cored, sliced 1/4 inch. Fronds are not an ingredient.

ingredients.name: orange
ingredients.note: zest and juice, about 1/3 cup juice. Divided: 2 tbsp juice on the fennel, the rest and all the zest at the end.

ingredients.name: olive oil
ingredients.note: tossed with the fennel. Not butter.

ingredients.name: kosher salt
ingredients.note: 1/2 tsp on the fennel, 1/4 tsp on the fish. Diamond Crystal. If Morton, use half.

steps.title: Roast the fennel
steps.body: Preheat the oven to 400 F. While it heats, toss the fennel with the olive oil, 1/2 tsp kosher salt, and 2 tbsp of the orange juice and spread it on a sheet pan. Once the oven is hot, roast 15 minutes, until the edges soften and start to brown. This is an oven roast. v1's method list said stovetop, and the steps never use a burner.

steps.title: Cook the char
steps.body: Pat the arctic char dry. Season with the remaining 1/4 tsp kosher salt and the black pepper. Nestle the fillets skin-side down on the fennel. Roast 10-12 minutes more, until the thickest part is just opaque, flakes with a fork, and reads 140-145 F. If a fillet is thinner than 1 inch, pull it at the early end of that range, still at just opaque. Not chalky.

steps.title: Finish
steps.body: Top with the fresh dill and the orange zest. Spoon on the remaining orange juice. Four servings, one fillet each.

projection.allergen_note: Finfish is an allergen, from the arctic char. It is not a dietary tag. Dairy-free is the dietary claim. This is not a plant dish.
